Hi Nina —

Great to be moving this forward. Quick notes from our side to make the private deployment runway as smooth as possible:

- We need your preferred VPC peering window (2–4 hour slot) and the target CIDR ranges for the peering session.
- Are you planning to use PrivateLink-style endpoints or VPC Peering only? Redwood Private supports both; we typically recommend Private Endpoints for minimal routing changes.
- Please attach any current firewall egress rules and proxy interceptors for the subnets that will call Redwood (we need outbound 443 to our Egress IP range).

Next steps: Rachel (CSM) will run a short technical intake with your infra team tomorrow. Marcus (implementation lead) will produce a draft connectivity checklist and a one-page runbook we can sign off together.

Attaching: initial checklist (draft) so you can see what we’ll cover.

Best,

On Wed, May 5, 2027 at 08:30 AM Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Nina / Rajesh —
>
> Thanks for the prompt answers and the attachments. Quick agenda for our 30-min intake (proposed):

Thanks — I pulled together a focused connectivity checklist that I’ll use during the call. Highlighted items we typically need to confirm:
- Egress IP range for your NAT gateway (for firewall allowlisting).
- Route table entries for PrivateLink (we need to confirm the per-AZ ENI placement).
- DNS zones: whether you’ll use private hosted zones pointing to our endpoint DNS name.
- MTU and jumbo frames (we’ve seen fragmentation with 1500 on some customer networks; call this out if you have non-standard).
- Expected token sizes / max sequence length for model payloads (so we can size TCP windowing).

I’ll post the checklist after the call and attach a draft runbook.

—Marcus

Hi all —

Thanks for the details, Rajesh — that gives us what we need. Attached is the first draft of the runbook (operational checklist + rollback), and a minimal firewall whitelist for the Private Endpoint activation. Highlights / agreed actions:
- Redwood will create the PrivateLink endpoint and share the per-AZ ENI names by EOD Tue May 11.
- Lighthouse will add outbound allow for 35.203.102.44/32 to port 443 and enable the internal CNAME redwood-private.lh -> our endpoint DNS.
- Cutover window confirmed: Thu May 13, 03:00–05:00 PT. Marcus will be on the bridge; Ben will coordinate post-cutover validation tests.
- Post-cutover: 48-hour monitor window. If we see >0.5% token error rate or latency spikes >95th percentile baseline, we will fallback to peering path and open a postmortem.

Please review the attached runbook and let me know any missing rollback steps. I’ll raise the HubSpot milestone to "Private Endpoint Provisioned" once you confirm.

Best,
Rachel
